{"self_assessment": "Impact: I sketched the fish plan on the pad: a back line from the tail round to the nose, with the belly branching off at the nose. I then laid the start domino and traced the whole back line, which carries the fall into everything else. I also laid the last stretch of the lower belly out to the tail tip. Before the push, the run traced by eye as fully connected, with all 125 dominoes standing in the chain.

Execution: I worked in a clear order: sketch, trace stroke 1, inspect the nose join, then lay stroke 3. I inspected the nose join and the middle of the belly closely before calling the run connected. Once everything was laid, I kept my hands off the table so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I split the long belly into two strokes so Sofia and I could build at the same time. I told her where to stop and picked up from that point. I kept the table updated on what I was laying, which stretches were done, and where the fall would run, so hands weren't doubled up on the same stretch. I asked others to check gaps and joins while I built.

Leadership: I made the call to go with a simple outline of two gentle curves, with the push starting at the tail end. I made sure everyone understood how the fall would travel before the belly was built. I proposed the stroke split, gave clear handoff points, and set the hands-off rule for the final minutes.", "my_share_percent": 35}
